title: 50 Rescued From Thane High-Rise Fire as Mumbai Records 89 Diwali Fire Calls
excerpt: Firefighters rescued 50 people from the Carlyle building in Thane's Raheja Garden complex on Diwali night with no casualties, while a Level-II fire hit Vidyavihar's Skyline Epitome and Mumbai logged 89 fire incidents over two days.
body:
• Fifty people were rescued and there were no casualties after fire broke out on the 8th, 9th and 10th floors of the Raheja Garden complex in Thane on Sunday night, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde said, according to ANI.
  • The Thane fire, at the 17-storey Carlyle building in Wagle Estate, was reported at 8:31 p.m.; two Bronto vehicles, two fire engines and tankers were deployed.
  • In Mumbai, a Level-II fire at the Skyline Epitome building in Vidyavihar was confined to floors seven to ten and declared at 12:52 a.m. on November 9.
  • Mumbai recorded 89 fire incidents over two Diwali days, 28 of them reportedly linked to firecrackers.

A major fire broke out on Diwali night at the Raheja Garden residential complex in Thane, and firefighters rescued 50 people with no casualties, officials said. The fire affected the 8th, 9th and 10th floors of the complex, ANI reported, and Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde reached the site and inspected the response.

"Our fire brigade personnel and TDR team acted with great courage; they risked their own lives to rescue people, successfully bringing 50 individuals to safety. There were zero casualties."

— Eknath Shinde, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister

The Thane rescue

The blaze was at the Carlyle building, a ground-plus-17-storey residential tower in the Raheja Garden complex in Wagle Estate, Thane West. The Thane Municipal Corporation's Regional Disaster Management Cell reported the incident at 8:31 p.m. on Sunday, with residents trapped inside, according to Urban Acres. Fire brigade personnel reached the complex with two Bronto fire vehicles, two fire engines, one water tanker and two jumbo water tankers, alongside disaster management, police and ambulance teams. Officials had not immediately established the cause of the fire. District Collector Shrikrushna Panchal, who also reached the building, said that following fire incidents allegedly linked to rockets during Diwali, a ban on rocket-style fireworks would be imposed effective from the next day, ANI reported.

A second tower fire in Vidyavihar

In Mumbai, a separate fire broke out at Skyline Epitome, a commercial building near Jolly Gymkhana in Vidyavihar, shortly before midnight. The fire was confined to the seventh to tenth floors of the ground-plus-10-storey building, and the Mumbai Fire Brigade declared it a Level-II fire call at 12:52 a.m. on November 9, The Daily Jagran reported.

89 incidents across Mumbai

The two tower fires came in a heavy two days for Mumbai's fire services. Mumbai recorded 89 fire incidents over two days during Diwali, with 28 cases reportedly linked to firecrackers. Other incidents were reported in Dongri, Powai, Virar, Mulund and Andheri West, and a 56-year-old security guard died due to suffocation inside a lift at Runwal Tower in Lokhandwala, according to reports of the two-day tally. In Thane, a second, smaller fire the same evening — in wooden decoration material stored on open ground near Mayur Building in Kopri, reported at 5:44 p.m. — was brought under control by about 6:25 p.m. with no injuries, civic officials said.
